Little Common come from behind to see off Pagham

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite falling behind early on, Common responded in excellent fashion, scoring twice before the break and adding two further goals in the second half to record a deserved victory.
  • Common started brightly and could have taken an early lead when Sam Ellis met a delivery into the box, only to see his header superbly saved by the visiting goalkeeper.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite falling behind early on, Common responded in excellent fashion, scoring twice before the break and adding two further goals in the second half to record a deserved victory.

Common started brightly and could have taken an early lead when Sam Ellis met a delivery into the box, only to see his header superbly saved by the visiting goalkeeper. However, it was Pagham who broke the deadlock in the 10th minute when Common failed to clear a free kick and the loose ball was scrambled home from close range.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The hosts looked for an immediate response and Ollie Hull went close to restoring parity, but his near-post effort was once again kept out by the busy Pagham goalkeeper.

Common's persistence was rewarded in spectacular fashion in the 23rd minute when Ollie MacDonald collected possession some 30 yards from goal before unleashing a thunderous strike that flew beyond the helpless goalkeeper and into the roof of the net.

The equaliser sparked Common into life and they soon completed the turnaround. Lewis Unwin delivered an inviting free kick into the penalty area, where Kieran Ludlow rose highest to guide a perfectly placed header into the far corner of the net.

Ludlow then demonstrated his importance at the opposite end, producing a vital goal-line clearance as Pagham searched for an equaliser.

Common had a golden opportunity to extend their advantage on the stroke of half-time when they were awarded a penalty. However, Hull saw his spot kick saved and appeared to be pulled down as he attempted to reach the rebound, only for the referee to wave away the appeals.

The hosts continued to look dangerous after the interval and extended their lead in the 57th minute. Excellent work from Hull down the left flank saw him deliver the ball across goal for Freddie Warren, who was on hand to tap home from close range.

Recent findings suggest that warren almost doubled his tally shortly afterwards when his effort crashed against the crossbar, while substitute Sonny Tyrell also went close after bursting into the penalty area, only to be denied by another fine save from the visiting goalkeeper. At the other end, Matt Cruttwell enjoyed a relatively quiet afternoon as Common defended resolutely and restricted Pagham to very few clear-cut opportunities.

Common put the icing on the cake in the 90th minute when Hull, who had been a constant threat throughout, once again turned provider. His pass found Tyrell on the edge of the penalty area and the substitute made no mistake, firing a powerful effort into the roof of the net to complete an emphatic victory.

Recent findings suggest that boss Russ Eldridge mentioned: “It was a massive three points for us and I felt we thoroughly deserved the win. Going behind early on was disappointing, particularly from a set piece, but the lads showed great character to respond in the way they did.

Sources indicate that “We scored some excellent goals, particularly Ollie MacDonald’s strike, a fantastic effort. We looked dangerous going forward and, in truth, could have scored a few more.

Recent findings suggest that “What pleased me most was the attitude and work rate. We’ve put in some really spirited performances against sides near the top of the table recently without getting rewards, so it was key we backed those up with three points.

According to recent reports, “We know there’s still plenty of hard work ahead of us, but hopefully this result will give everyone a bit of confidence and something to build on. The challenge now is to put a run of results together.”.

Common host Midhurst on Saturday (Nov 28).

  • Andoni Iraola's men have taken nine points from 12 on offer in Europe so far, good enough for eighth place in the Champions League rankings after their 3-2 loss to Fenerbahce last time out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 22:00, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 22:00.

Liverpool go on the hunt for a fourth win from five Champions League matches on Wednesday evening, when the Reds take on Club Brugge at the Jan Breydel Stadion.

Andoni Iraola's men have taken nine points from 12 on offer in Europe so far, good enough for eighth place in the Champions League rankings after their 3-2 loss to Fenerbahce last time out.

The Reds also return to European action on the back of a 4-0 demolition of Manchester United, rising into the top four of the Premier League table in the process.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their showdown with Club Brugge, who are just one place below Liverpool in the 36-team table courtesy of an inferior goals scored total.

Possible return date: November 29 (vs. Everton).

Cody Gakpo was a surprise absentee from the Liverpool squad against Man United, and Iraola subsequently revealed that the attacker had picked up a calf injury on Netherlands duty.

Gakpo is also expected to miss out in midweek, but there is a chance that he could recover in time for next weekend's Merseyside derby.

Industry observers note that possible return date: November 25 (vs. Club Brugge).

Sunday's game against Man Utd came too soon for Ryan Gravenberch to return from a heel injury, but the midfielder might be able to make his comeback on Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Hugo Ekitike is making continued progress in his rehabilitation from a serious Achilles injury, but the French striker is still expected to miss the rest of 2026.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Out for over a year with a serious knee injury, Giovanni Leoni returned to team training during the international break and is now in the "last part" of his recovery process, but a playing comeback before the Fresh Year is still incredibly unlikely.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Likewise, Conor Bradley is finally back with his teammates on the training pitches after sustaining a severe knee problem in January, but it will be a few more weeks before he is considered for selection too.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

In a recent development, after thirty four weeks we finally have a home league win to enjoy. What a ridiculous amount of time to wait, but boy it was worth the wait. Fleetwood, the team that beat Arsenal recently in the League Cup, loses to the mighty Crawley Town at a euphoric Broadfield Stadium.

According to recent reports, A performance and a victory was the perfect way to put the Wimborne FA Cup shambles behind us. Newly appointed Reds gaffer Kevin Blackwell was grinning from ear to ear at full time with a victory that puts us to within three points of safety. All of a sudden we have a team with momentum. Two well taken goals from Kai Jennings and Pemi Aderoju put us two up, and even though the cod army pulled one back, we got the job done and sent the majority of the three thousand plus crowd home happy.

The new centre half pairing of Josh Flint and Ben Heneghan were superb and mopped up everything that Fleetwood threw at them.

Sources indicate that the energy and commitment by a squad short on confidence was there for all to see. The victory means we have now picked up seven points from a possible nine. With the games now coming thick and fast with points aplenty up for grabs. It’s been a disaster of a start to a season, but the signs are clear that things are changing. The decision by the club to appoint interim manager Kevin Blackwell as gaffer to the end of the season is an absolute masterstroke by the club. The contacts and connections KB has in the game will be key to guiding us to EFL safety. The signing of experienced Premier League forward Connor Wickham screams Kevin Blackwell’s influence all day long. The lack of physicality in the squad is finally being addressed. We were left in a completely mess by Erdem and Kazim, who thought they were building a squad to compete. In reality they had built a squad to strangle us.

In a recent development, good riddance to bad eggs. We can finally move forward as one and start winning football matches again. A United Crawley Town is a machine to fear. The whole of the EFL League Two needs to take note and realise the Reds are in the rise once again. Now let’s kick on and get ourselves up the football league table.

#95478. Breaking: Ian Hart: Let’s keep Brighton’s defeat to Tigers in perspective – and get back on the horse quickly

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (626 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Ian Hart: Let’s keep Brighton’s defeat to Tigers in perspective – and get back on the horse quickly

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • No matter how much possession you have or how many chances you create, or what the xG is (whatever that is!), unless you put the ball over the line more times than your opponents, it ultimately counts for nothing.
  • But while Sunday’s defeat at Hull City wasn’t pleasant viewing, perhaps in almost a perverse way it might be the wake-up call the Albion needed.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No matter how much possession you have or how many chances you create, or what the xG is (whatever that is!), unless you put the ball over the line more times than your opponents, it ultimately counts for nothing.

But while Sunday’s defeat at Hull City wasn’t pleasant viewing, perhaps in almost a perverse way it might be the wake-up call the Albion needed.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Industry observers note that let’s admit it, in the lead-up to the most recent international break, we were almost getting carried away. Full disclosure I, among thousands of others, was secretly daring to dream, maybe not the title, but the words Champions and League had entered old Harty’s thought process.

And to be fair that wasn’t just from within the club and its fanbase, externally, Brighton were being lauded as legitimate title contenders.

While attending an excellent Seagulls Down Under function in Adelaide, one of the Albion’s ever-growing Aussie contingent revealed me an online tabloid story stating that Brighton would be head to head with defending Champions Arsenal for the League!

Some weeks ago I wrote that I felt Albion more suited to the role of ‘EPL ‘andlords’ in that while they might not win the title, along with the likes of Bournemouth and Brentford they would ultimately dictate the outcome of the competition.

And after Sunday, that might also apply at the other end of the table.

Prior to kick-off, Hull City only had Manchester United below them in the form table. While there are still 27 games to go, that last-gasp and – many might argue – somewhat fortunate win for the Tigers, might be the difference between success and failure come the end of the season.

Given the Albion should have been home and hosed by half-time, it is extremely annoying, but it’s football.

And the next 270 minutes, with the Albion playing three games in seven days – the Conference League home tie against Romania’s Universitatea Craiova on Thursday night, before league games on Sunday and Wednesday, Newcastle at home and Bournemouth away – I believe we will see and learn more about the character of Fabian Hurzeler and his squad.

With those games and the welcome return of the talismanic Kaoru Mitoma from his long-term injury, it’s very much of a case of getting back on the horse immediately and moving forward again.

I do wonder how much the attendance on Thursday will be affected by the 5.45pm kick-off time, to accommodate the TV companies. However perhaps on the flip.side with it being a ‘school night’ with a sensible ticket pricing policy we might see a number of the next generation of young Albion fans attending the Amex for the first time.

We will know the answer to that around 7pm Thursday and hopefully by then the Albion will be well on the way to returning to winning ways.

As a footnote, and another opportunity to put things firmly into perspective, Sunday’s game on Humberside was a couple of weeks short of the 30th anniversary of perhaps one of the most memorable Brighton v Hull fixtures.

Saturday, December 14, 1996 – Steve Gritt’s first game as Albion manager, with his new charges firmly rooted to the bottom of the entire Football League.

Anti-Gritt graffiti outside the ground (with his name spelt wrong!), a fans’ protest involving 3,000 whistles to put the poor old ref on the back foot, but in the end a 3-0 and ‘The Great Escape’ was on!

So all these years later, despite Sunday’s defeat, the Albion are still second in the Premier League doesn’t seem that bad.

#95477. Man City are failing to give their supporters something to stand behind as Enzo Maresca's side radiate uncertainty with meek display in Fulham draw, writes JACK GAUGHAN

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (924 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Man City are failing to give their supporters something to stand behind as Enzo Maresca's side radiate uncertainty with meek display in Fulham draw, writes JACK GAUGHAN

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (924 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:04 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:16 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • The bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week.
  • Sources indicate that city were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:04 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:16 EST, 21 November 2026.

The bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week. In legal limbo, Manchester City’s supporters need something – anything – to stand behind but increasingly their team refuse to provide that solace.

Sources indicate that city were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel. Some of that could have been directed at referee Thomas Bramall, after Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal, but certainly a significant number were jeering what they’d just seen. That simply does not happen at the Etihad Stadium, even during the torrid run of two years ago.

But they are witnessing a squad who radiate uncertainty. Who take three touches when two will do; who always receive possession squarely facing their own goal; who do not create passing lines for their mates. And crucially, who are forever momentarily confused as to who exactly is picking up which runner and those split seconds make all the difference in this division.

In a recent development, there is just this strange state of unease around how they want to approach games at the moment, something that adversity can provoke and something that Maresca is adamant he can correct. A coach of his calibre should do given the time and freedom.

Yet when he spent the two-week international break studying clips and fashioning ways of improving, he cannot have envisaged a scenario whereby home fans were so incredulous at a lack of energy that they were roused to their feet when Haaland deigned to close down Bernd Leno and force an error.

Man City put in an underwhelming performance as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham.

Enzo Maresca's side are radiating uncertainty and look worryingly vulnerable at the back.

Rodrigo Muniz made City pay as he put an impressive Fulham 1-0 ahead after 16 minutes.

Fulham popped it about nicely and at will. Found pockets to hurt their illustrious hosts, who were again asking a centre half – in this case Marc Guehi – to charge into midfield. City did have more balance than at Nottingham Forest for including Ayyoub Bouaddi for Enzo Fernandez, yet Alvaro Arbeloa still aggressively pressed them in that area to some success.

‘I told the players that we will have the chance to beat them if we play with courage,’ stated Arbeloa, who was indebted to the towering performance of defender David Affengruber.

Arsenal will have watched this grinning and could easily be racking up an unassailable lead once these teams meet in north London next Sunday. Unassailable with all the usual caveats about the appeal and what this season may or may not eventually mean.

City did create enough statistically but as with other games of late, that did not tell the whole story.

Calvin Bassey pirouetted through midfield, the heavily derided Gianluigi Donnarumma thwarting a number of strong Fulham chances, and City appeared somewhat lost and out of ideas.

Elliot Anderson equalised with a superb volley but City failed to create much after that.

Maresca expressed his concern at City's lack of clean sheets after they struggled again.

That is a worrying departure from recent defeats, where they attacked with the same abandon as that early season flourish when they might as well have hosted games at Madison Square Gardens and played with an orange ball.

MAN CITY (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 7; Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Guehi 5, O’Reilly 5 (Gvardiol 78); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 7 (Fernandez 85); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 78), Foden 7 (Cherki 70), Doku 5; Haaland 5.

FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Leno 6; Tete 6, Affengruber 8, Bassey 7, Sessegnon 7 (Palacios 83); Berge 6, Charles 7; Bobb 7 (Garcia 78), King 6 (Larsson 70, 6), Iwobi 7 (Robinson 70, 6); Muniz 7 (Cairney 83).

Met with a Fulham who had not conceded more than once in the league since the start of September, City failed to create a meaningful opportunity in the last 25 minutes of a match they were desperate to win and should have been in the ascendancy of after Elliot Anderson’s volleyed equaliser after half time.

Maresca, though, is more concerned with a lack of clean sheets. It’s now none of those in nine games in all competitions for the first time in seven years, with Rodrigo Muniz opening the scoring on 16 minutes. A throw inside Fulham’s own third prompted Guehi to jump and lose his duel, City turned around and Oscar Bobb laid on for Muniz.

According to recent reports, ‘We’re conceding too many goals,’ Maresca said. ‘We need to avoid it. You need to win games 1-0. You need clean sheets. We’re not able to do it. But I can see many positive aspects. We started four months ago and not four years ago.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We’ve conceded almost 80 per cent of our goals at the start of the first half and second half. It’s something we need to improve. It’s a throw in at the corner flag and nobody is expecting they can create something.’.

Maresca was also insistent that Haaland ought to have been awarded an equaliser before the break when poking in on the goal line, yet Bramall adjudged that Leno had the ball under control on field, with VAR not overruling.

Some hard luck, some profligacy with Haaland squandering a couple of substantial chances, but the day was summed up when in stoppage time, Jeremy Doku was penalised for a foul throw.

By Anthony Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 23:17, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 05:02.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of his first Champions League game in the Manchester United dugout on Wednesday, when the team travel to face Sporting Lisbon in Portugal.

The Red Devils were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool on Sunday, and are looking to Europe for a reprieve from their domestic woes.

Pochettino started Patrick Dorgu and brought Harry Maguire on as a substitute at Anfield, though he remains without a significant number of players ahead of this midweek clash.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up all of Man United's injury and suspension news ahead of their Champions League showdown with Sporting.

Industry observers note that possible return date: December 2 (vs. Newcastle United).

Midfielder Carlos Baleba was forced off with a hamstring injury during United's 3-2 win over Roma last time out in the Champions League, and is eyeing a return to action in early December.

Possible return date: December 2 (vs. Newcastle).

Marcus Rashford has been out of action since a lingering hip problem spread to his groin last month, and he is unlikely to feature on Wednesday after missing the Liverpool game.

Possible return date: November 25 (vs. Sporting Lisbon).

Left-back Luke Shaw has been sidelined since United's 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur on October 10, and though he missed the defeat to Liverpool, his return to training suggests he could be in with a chance of making the squad on Wednesday.

Striker Benjamin Sesko has been dealing with a recurring shin injury that he initially developed towards the end of the 2025-26 campaign, and while he was thought to be closing in on a return this autumn, his recovery timeline has reportedly slipped closer to the start of 2027.

Defensive midfielder Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious knee injury during World Cup 2026, and is likely to be sidelined until the spring after undergoing surgery and rehabilitation.

Versatile forward Matheus Cunha was the hero of United's win against Roma, but he was sent off late in the game after receiving a second yellow card for his celebrations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have played six Premier League games this season and Bruno Guimarães has been a match-winning force in two of them. At this rate, he might justify his enormous £75m transfer fee by Christmas.

According to recent reports, the Brazilian was not signed to be Arsenal’s super sub but that is the role he appears to be playing in these early days in north London. Against Leeds United here, as it was against Sunderland last month, he came off the bench when the champions were struggling. And as it was at Sunderland, he produced a thumping finish to put Arsenal on their way to three points.

Liquid football from Arsenal 😮‍💨 Bruno Guimarães finishes off a well-worked team move! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/fbLJiaZbX5.

Sources indicate that this is the value of signing a 28-year-old with significant Premier League experience. As Arsenal laboured against an impressively organised and courageous Leeds side, Mikel Arteta knew that Guimarães was capable of coming into the game and adjusting to its demands. There has been no adaptation period required for Guimarães, who is fast becoming one of the most popular players in north London.

The finish, which put Arsenal 2-1 ahead at the Emirates Stadium, marked an emphatic conclusion to a fabulous passing sequence. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice all combined at speed before Guimarães charged on to Rice’s flick. “It was a beauty,” mentioned Arteta of the goal. The move had actually begun at the feet of Guimarães a few moments earlier, when he nutmegged an opponent in style.

The winning goal came just eight minutes after Riccardo Calafiori, Arsenal’s thrilling left-back/centre-forward hybrid, had pulled them level in the game. James Justin had struck for Leeds shortly after half-time, creating a horrible anxiety among the home fans here, and for much of the afternoon Daniel Farke’s side were the better team.

It has been revealed that leeds finally have their opener! 🤩 James Justin arrives at the back post to fire them ahead. 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/ITjUMSlrG1.

Sources indicate that leeds, though, could not compete with Arsenal for depth. The arrival of Guimarães as a 63rd-minute substitute represented a flexing of Arteta’s managerial muscle, in his first match since signing a fresh long-term contract, and the Brazilian offered a moment of attacking quality that his opponents were unable to replicate.

It has been revealed that it was actually the first competitive home game that Guimarães had played for Arsenal since his transfer from Newcastle United, as a result of a few niggles and the club’s unusual run of four consecutive away matches before the international break. The most recent of those was the 3-0 thrashing by Brighton, which was one of their worst defeats of the last few seasons.

This gritty victory represented a necessary response to that defeat, even if the performance was far from dominant. “We had a point to prove,” said Arteta. “Something was touched in our identity against Brighton.”.

Guimarães, too, clearly felt that some wrongs needed to be made right. For all his brilliance in this game and against Sunderland, he had produced a horrible showing at the Amex Stadium a few weeks ago. “He was not at that level against Brighton,” stated Arteta. “This is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action you have to be at that level. At Brighton, he wasn’t. Today, he was much better.”.

Industry observers note that leeds had not lost in their opening five Premier League matches of this season and it was easy to see why. They were willing to press Arsenal high up the pitch, taking risks and engaging in physical duels, and the strategy proved hugely effective for an hour.

If they had been more precise in the final third, they could have been a few goals ahead by the time Justin converted Gabriel Gudmundsson’s left-wing cross after 55 minutes. Anton Stach, who was accidentally blocked by team-mate Jayden Bogle, and Gudmundsson both went close in the first half.

David Raya at his very best to deny Leeds the opener 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/hOB8RMapxw.

“I am heartbroken and gutted for my players,” mentioned Farke. “They deserved to travel back with points today. The defeat has to do with the quality of the players they [Arsenal] could bring in. It is down to the mentality Mikel has created here that even on a tough day they find a way to win the game.”.

In a recent development, the early kick-off, the long international break, the slow start and the memories of the Brighton defeat made it a strange atmosphere at the Emirates. You would not have known they were the champions, based on the reaction of the fans to the first-half performance, but the achievements of last season clearly do not guarantee fervent support at all times.

Industry observers note that calafiori’s equaliser, which marked his fifth goal involvement in 10 games for club and country this season, changed the momentum of the game. The Italian is such an unusual player but this was a simple goal, converted from close range after Ben White had headed the ball back across the penalty area. “The energy changed immediately,” stated Arteta.

It has been revealed that from that moment on, it was a matter of time before Arsenal found their second. On came Guimarães, Viktor Gyokeres, Jurrien Timber, and the home side suddenly had renewed energy. Saka, Odegaard and Rice found each other in a flowing move, before Guimarães powered his low finish into the corner of James Trafford’s net. “That is the quality that is needed at this level,” said Arteta.

Before the game we talked about two things, the challenge ahead against a team that had not lost in the Premier League. They full deserved to be where they are and it was going to be really tough. The second was to restore our identity and be ourselves again.

We weren’t pleased with our performance against Brighton and we wanted to put it right. But the context is that this was a difficult one [opponent]. But we reacted in a way that was unique and made it so special.

[Leeds] are very well organised, very physical and very committed in everything that they do. They are a threat. They are incredible the way they attack the ball and set-pieces, with belief. They came close to punishing us. They have individual quality and they are in a good moment.

According to recent reports, when you play at 12.30 at home and you go one-nil down there’s a lot to do. You have to restore a lot of things. Energy is one of them. We had an incredible response. The crowd changed. You could see it.

In a recent development, we brought a lot of leadership on [with his three subs]. We brought goal threat, to win duels, people who can play forward and penetrate against their high press.

The timing, movement and execution of it [the winning goal], yes, it was a beauty.

Unbelievable. Against Brighton we were not at the level. This was all about bouncing back. This is my first official game at home. Great finish, I am very happy. My job if on the bench is to give a headache to the manager.

I have been proving myself in the Premier League but it was crucial for me today.

Leeds have a great team, a top game. Glad we could get the three points.

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

Match Report by Tom Coleman-Fry.

After nine games in all competitions without a victory, Three Bridges finally revealed signs of life, securing a much-needed 2-1 win over Cheshunt in what was a crucial encounter for their survival hopes.

According to recent reports, following a more encouraging performance against Dartford on Tuesday evening, Bridges knew that nothing less than three points would do if they were to stand any chance of remaining a Step 3 side next season. And it was the home side who started on the front foot, dominating much of the first half and creating a number of opportunities. Noel Leighton, Reece Hallard, Hayden Velvick and Charlie Bennett all went close inside the opening 25 minutes, but none could find a way past Cheshunt goalkeeper Rex Porter.

Recent findings suggest that against the run of play, however, the visitors took the lead. Hayden Neathey conceded a needless free-kick just outside the penalty area, and Joe Re stepped up to curl the ball past Sam Roberts. That familiar sinking feeling descended over Jubilee Field, and despite having enjoyed the better of the half, Bridges went into the interval a goal behind.

But this time, there was no heads dropping. Bridges continued where they had left off, and their positive approach was eventually rewarded.

After seeing an attempted lob saved by Porter, Leighton and his teammates finally found a way through, with the lively HAYDEN VELVICK restoring parity. Picking up the ball on the right-hand side of the penalty area, the winger unleashed an effort which somehow found its way past Porter at his near post. However it went in, nobody in amber and black was complaining, and Bridges were back on level terms.

The hosts continued to press for a winner, and debutant Jadyn Dundas should have put them ahead just minutes after coming off the bench. Arriving at the back post with the goal at his mercy, he was unable to get his feet sorted out in time to convert. What then followed was an end-to-end contest, with Sam Granville striking the crossbar for Cheshunt before Leighton and Velvick both saw efforts bravely blocked by visiting defenders.

Industry observers note that this time, though, Bridges were not to be denied. Cheshunt failed to deal with the danger inside their own penalty area, and after Porter could only parry an initial deflected effort, the ball fell kindly into the path of NOEL LEIGHTON. The striker made no mistake from close range, sending Jubilee Field into celebration and, more importantly, putting Bridges 2-1 ahead.

The home side looked relatively comfortable heading towards the final whistle, but injury time brought one final scare. An almighty scramble inside the Bridges six-yard box threatened to produce a late Cheshunt equaliser, with the visitors seemingly doing everything they could to force the ball over the line. Somehow, the Bridges defence stood firm and managed to clear their lines before the referee finally blew for full-time.

Sources indicate that there was an enormous sigh of relief around Jubilee Field as Three Bridges secured just their third league victory of the season. A hugely important result for Jamie Crellin's side, and one which could prove to be a turning point in their season.

If the great escape is to become a reality, Jubilee Field must now become a fortress, starting next Saturday afternoon when Wingate & Finchley visit for another crucial encounter.

Bridges team: Roberts, Ferreira, J Hallard (Irving 75), Adeyinka, Neathey, Leighton (C), R Hallard (Dundas 65), Malone, Saunders, Velvick, Bennett (Idowu-Johnson 87).

Unused Subs: Villavicencio, Przybylo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derek McInnes insists the prospect of lifting the Premier Sports Cup in the coming weeks has his squad operating with laser-like focus, with Saturday’s dramatic late victory over Motherwell providing a further boost to their growing belief that trophies are within reach.

There is still plenty of work to be done before the Rangers can contemplate silverware, but McInnes believes a shot at Hampden glory is acting as an added incentive for his players and is helping to drive standards inside the dressing room.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Before their return trip to the national stadium on December 13, Rangers must navigate a favourable-looking sequence of home fixtures, with Aberdeen, Falkirk and Dundee United all due to visit Ibrox over the next eight days in the Scottish Premiership.

While the cup final represents an obvious carrot and a major opportunity for silverware is fast approaching, McInnes knows it is impossible for his players to ignore the occasion altogether. However, he is equally determined to ensure their focus remains on the immediate task in hand, claiming performances over the next four league fixtures could determine who earns the right to feature when the substantial occasion arrives.

Speaking after his side kept their Premiership title assault firmly on track with a last-gasp success at Fir Park, McInnes mentioned: “I don't think I'll mention it too often, but they are not daft, they see that and everybody wants to play in the team. Anybody who's in the team needs to keep playing well to stay in the team and anybody who's not in the team needs to train right and take advantage of their minutes.

In a recent development, “We make that point often enough. Sometimes you've got to come away to tough venues like Motherwell and do the hard work and get the reward, but there's bigger games like a cup final looming, so everybody wants to play in that one. I'm sure it does us no harm. It keeps the fans bubbling along, a chance of silverware, so when it comes along hopefully we're in good form.”.

If the celebrations following Ryan Naderi’s scrappy 88th-minute winner against the Steelmen were anything to go by, a turbo-charged belief is surging through the Rangers ranks as they look to end a two-season trophy drought.

Such resilience is invaluable in a title challenge and McInnes is encouraged by that quality, but stressed the need for greater consistency in his side’s performance levels leading to those decisive moments.

It has been revealed that “I think we're the only team in the Premier League who's not lost away from home, but we understand that draws won't get the job done,” he stated. “Last-minute winners are brilliant. They're normally aligned with successful teams and they can get so many points from that. It's good to know that we've got that but, like I say, I wouldn't want to be depending on it far too often.”.

According to recent reports, the importance of Rangers’ upcoming run of home fixtures is not lost on McInnes. While the jubilant scenes at full-time in North Lanarkshire were particularly satisfying, there was little time to revel in the celebrations with Aberdeen arriving at Ibrox on Tuesday night.

The Dons will venture back down the A90 in buoyant mood after giving fresh boss Mario Frick a winning start to his Pittodrie tenure with a 4-2 victory over bottom club Kilmarnock at the weekend.

Industry observers note that the long-standing rivalry between the clubs leaves McInnes in no doubt that his side face another demanding test against his former club. Nevertheless, he is relishing a return to familiar surroundings after a run of five consecutive away matches.

He is equally aware, however, that home advantage alone offers no guarantee of success.

Recent findings suggest that “It's unusual with five games now away from Ibrox, four in the league and the cup game, and now the fixtures kind of run the other way,” McInnes mentioned. “We've got some good fixtures at home but we always look at little blocks in the week, and where we're looking to try and get to by a certain period, get certain points and certain targets.

It has been revealed that “There was obviously a lot of joy and pleasure with that [Motherwell result], but it wasn't over the top. When we spoke after the game, it was about getting ourselves ready for Aberdeen. We all know the historical rivalry between both clubs. I’m sure they'll come to Ibrox with a bit of confidence getting the result [against Kilmarnock]. We need to be ready for that.

Recent findings suggest that “We’ve got a substantial week ahead of us. and we've got to make sure we're a strong home team again. Hopefully we can score a few more goals but, ultimately, as long as we win the game I'll be happy.”.

  • Homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives.
  • Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives. The substantial-brained, tool-wielding species emerged two million years ago in Africa and expanded across Eurasia, before vanishing around 100,000 years ago in Java, Indonesia.

Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

In a recent development, did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

According to recent reports, researchers have now added another feather to the hominin’s cap. A pair of studies analysing fossil teeth1,2, which were published in Nature on 18 November, suggest that H. erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago.

Researchers had thought that H. erectus was limited to savannahs and open woodlands, states Kira Westaway, a geochronologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, and a co-author of both studies.

It has been revealed that “Never, ever have we seen them in rainforests,” she adds. “This is a really substantial deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

The earliest H. erectus fossils, from eastern Africa, are 1.9 million years old. But the svelte, upright-walking and running hominins wasted little time, reaching western Asia and present-day China some 200,000 years later and modern Java, using land bridges, not long after. The last-known H. erectus remains, from central Java, date to roughly 110,000 years ago3.

Limestone caves in Guangxi province, southern China, contained more than 10,000 fossil teeth.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

According to recent reports, while looking for fossils from a three-metre-tall great ape called Gigantopithecus, Westaway and her colleagues identified a pair of limestone caves in Guangxi province in southern China. There, they discovered more than 10,000 fossil teeth from animals such as orangutans (Pongo spp.), monkeys and wild boar (Sus spp.), as well as 9 from hominins. The researchers estimate that the hominins lived between 184,000 and 324,000 years ago, according to dating of both fossils and the surrounding sediments using various methods.

Eight of the hominin teeth resembled those of H. erectus in their shape, a designation that was confirmed by analysing the sequences of proteins preserved in the dental enamel of four specimens, says co-author Frido Welker, a molecular palaeoanthropologist at the University of Copenhagen.

The tooth enamel was analysed and its proteins sequenced.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

The ninth lacked the shape and protein signature of H. erectus teeth, indicates Welker, and it also didn’t resemble those of H. sapiens or Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis). Denisovans — enigmatic ancient humans first discovered in southern Siberia and now linked to diverse fossils from China and elsewhere in Asia — are a possibility, but the evidence is circumstantial, says Welker. “Every label we put on that ninth tooth is a little bit of speculation.”.

The multitude of animal teeth was probably accumulated by a scavenger such as a porcupine. The presence of fossils from species such as muntjac deer (Muntiacus muntjac), leopards and orangutans hints at a rainforest environment.

By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 23:34, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 01:54.

Fulham defender Calvin Bassey has confirmed he is in negotiations to extend his contract despite interest from Manchester United this January.

The Red Devils were resoundingly beaten by Liverpool on Sunday, losing 4-0 at Anfield, with defender Leny Yoro receiving an early red card.

Mauricio Pochettino has only been leading the club since Wednesday, but he will already be aware of the need to address the team's defensive frailties, especially as they are 19th in the Premier League table with just eight points after 11 matchweeks.

The Red Devils have been linked with centre-back Bassey, but the defender confirmed that he is in discussions to extend his deal with Fulham, telling TNT Sports: "We’re still negotiating, we’re still talking and obviously it’s an amazing place to be.

According to recent reports, I’ve settled in nicely and the manager has put a lot of faith and trust in me. So, it’s nice to be here and hopefully we will see what happens with the negotiations.".

Bassey's current deal is set to expire in 2027, though Fulham have an option to extend his stay by a year, so news that the 26-year-old is hopeful of further extending his time at Craven Cottage will come as a blow to Pochettino.

It has been revealed that “Just proud of the boys today, you know how hard it is to play here” Calvin Bassey and David Affengruber reflect on a huge point for Fulham away at the Etihad ? ? Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Szb8cvHyJ6.

Bassey is a strong channel defender and is much more athletic than United's current options at the back, something that has been a major issue this season.

Harry Maguire is now 33 and his mobility problems have only worsened as he has aged, while Lisandro Martinez has never been suited to playing in an aggressive, high-pressing system.

Yoro is young enough to contribute in the coming seasons, but he has not developed since signing for the club in July 2024.

The Premier League is the most physically and mentally demanding league in the world, and signing someone with experience of the top flight would be hugely beneficial.

The reservations that some have at the club about Bassey's place in the XI in the years to come should not matter given the real threat of relegation.

United would have ended Sunday bottom of the league had Crystal Palace beaten Coventry City on Saturday, and the fixture schedule does not get any easier for the Red Devils.

With games against Brentford, Newcastle United, Coventry, Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland to come before the end of the year, Pochettino's side cannot afford to drop many points if they wish to avoid the one-point gap to safety increasing.

Isaac Brown, returning from injury, replaced Rob Deda with Oliver Deda switching to the left of defence.

Celtic midfielder Benjamin Nygren is on the radar of Atalanta and Bologna, according to reports in Italy.

Nygren joined Celtic from FC Nordsjaelland in the summer of 2025 for a fee in the region of £1.5 million and made a big impact, scoring 21 goals across all competitions as the champions retained their Premiership crown and also lifted the Scottish Cup.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The 25-year-old also represented Sweden earlier this year at the World Cup and remains an integral part of Graham Potter’s international squad.

This season, Nygren has netted eight times in 21 games. And with the January transfer window approaching, it is understood that two Serie A clubs in Atalanta and Bologna are weighing up a bid for Nygren.

Respected Italian transfer journalist Gianluca di Marzio has claimed in an interview with Rekatochklart that a move could be made for Nygren on the back of his performances over the past 18 months,.

According to recent reports, “Nygren is a very good player and Atalanta like him a lot, but they haven’t made a move for him yet,” stated Di Marzio. “He is a target and they are following him.

“Bologna like him too, but no negotiations have started yet. They follow him because he is doing very well both for Celtic and Sweden.”.

Bologna have taken an active interest over the past few years in the Scottish market, signing defender Aaron Hickey from Hearts and midfielder Lewis Ferguson from Aberdeen.

Atalanta were also very interested in Matt O’Riley before the Celtic midfielder moved to Brighton and Hove Albion rather than Serie A in 2024.

Nygren admitted in September that there was interest in him after the World Cup this summer, although nothing materialised for the Swede.

Industry observers note that “Yeah, there was interest,” he remarked. “Was it more than that? No, I play for a substantial club. When the right time is to move on, I cannot answer that. That’s up to me, the club and the potential club. So whenever the right time is, it is.

Sources indicate that “I play for a huge club like Celtic. I really enjoy being here. I wanted to stay here to play in the biggest competition. Unfortunately, we didn’t make it to the Champions League, but we still play in the Europa League. I want to make it better here and then go further in the Europa League that we did last season.

According to recent reports, “I wanted to stay here and continue to make it good and when the right time is, the right time is. But it’s not something I think of now. It’s not my focus. My focus is just to do as well as possible here and to win more trophies and then what happens in the future, we’ll see.”.

Nygren is contracted to Celtic until 2030 and the Premiership leaders would likely demand a hefty fee for his services.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hampden and Easter Road are set to host Women’s World Cup matches after England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales were confirmed as the joint hosts of the 2035 edition of the tournament.

The four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It will be the first men’s or women’s World Cup finals to be staged in the UK since the 1966 men’s tournament was held in England.

Recent findings suggest that nineteen stadiums are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams. One of those venues – Old Trafford – has been included in its current guise but any rebuilt stadium is envisaged to be a host.

A further three stadiums could be added – Birmingham’s newly introduced Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea stadium – which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 stadiums across the four nations.

Scotland have two Candidate Stadiums - the national football arena Hampden (capacity 52,032), which was used as part of the delayed Euro 2020 men’s tournament in 2021, and Easter Road, the home of Hibs with a capacity of 20,093, that has never been used for a major tournament.

The bid team projected the tournament would attract 3.5 billion viewers worldwide, and that 4.5 million tickets would be sold.

FIFA’s evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

The Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

Commenting on confirmation that Scotland will co-host the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035, First Minister John Swinney stated:.

Recent findings suggest that "This is fantastic news for Scotland. We have proved time and again that we are a world-class host, and I am delighted that the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035 will be held in Scotland alongside England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

“The timing is ideal. Project 2035, our upcoming long-term plan to grow the girls' and women's game, aims to establish Scotland as a leading nation for women's football by 2035. Our newly established girls’ and women’s football taskforce will help to make this happen, capitalising on the World Cup and leaving a lasting legacy for communities across the country.

Recent findings suggest that “Scotland is building a remarkable reputation for hosting major events, and the FIFA Women’s World Cup joins the Tour de France Grand Départ, The Open, the World Rally Championships and UEFA EURO 2028 in promising to showcase what our country has to offer. We will make sure each one of these amazing sporting events delivers for our economy, supporting jobs, businesses and tourism.”.

English Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt addressed the Congress after the bid’s success had been confirmed.

“Thank you for your trust and confidence in awarding us the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035,” Hewitt said.

“We’re deeply honoured by your support and grateful for the opportunity to host the pinnacle of women’s football on behalf of the global football family.

“As we said throughout our bid, we want this to be your FIFA Women’s World Cup, a World Cup for everyone.

“Together, we will celebrate the power of women’s football, inspire the next generation, and unite fans from every corner of the world. We look forward to welcoming you to the United Kingdom in 2035 and just as importantly, to working closely with you all in the years ahead to deliver an exceptional FIFA Women’s World Cup that the entire football community can be proud of.”.

Scotland’s World Cup award can be game-changing for the nation

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scotland captain Caroline Weir claims the country being named as a host nation for the 2035 Women’s World Cup is a “pivotal moment” for the sport.
  • The United Kingdom’s four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.
  • Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scotland captain Caroline Weir claims the country being named as a host nation for the 2035 Women’s World Cup is a “pivotal moment” for the sport.

The United Kingdom’s four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Nineteen stadiums are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams.

Industry observers note that while the 2022 European Championships were held in England, Scotland has never hosted a major women’s football event. Hampden Park in Glasgow (capacity 52,032) and Hibs’ Easter Road in Edinburgh (capacity 20,093) are Scotland’s Candidate Stadiums and would stage at least group-stage matches. Weir feels that having the competition on Scotland’s doorstep will show youngsters in this country that “anything is possible”.

Midfielder Weir, who currently plays for Lyon and has won 122 caps for Scotland, stated: “Hosting the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup in the UK is a pivotal moment for women’s football in this country. Playing at the 2019 Women’s World Cup in France was an incredible moment in my career, so knowing that the next generation of Scottish players will have the chance to experience that on home soil is so special.

“The women's game in Scotland has so much potential and this tournament is a real opportunity to drive momentum and help take it to another level both nationally and internationally.

“For young girls and boys across the country, seeing the best players in the world right on their doorstep will show them that anything is possible.

“We’re so proud to play our part in welcoming the world in 2035 and I know I speak on behalf of all of the players and staff when I say that we are ready to rise to the challenge and help deliver a truly memorable, world-class tournament.”.

Recent findings suggest that scottish Football chief executive Ian Maxwell hailed the decision to award the event to the UK. “Securing the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup alongside our Home Nations partners is a momentous milestone for Scottish football,” he said. “Scotland has a proud footballing heritage and a rapidly growing women’s game, and welcoming the world to Barclays Hampden and Easter Road will turbo-charge the progress we have made across our grassroots, domestic, and international game.

“This tournament will be the single-biggest sporting event ever staged in the UK, and our ambition goes far beyond the matches themselves. It gives us a powerful platform to inspire participation in a new generation of girls and women across Scotland, empower more female leaders and match officials and deliver a sustainable commercial and community legacy for many years to come.”.

It will be the first time that Easter Road, the home of Hibs, has been selected to host a major international event and the club say they are hugely excited at the prospect.

Hibs Women’s head coach Joelle Murray said: “This is fantastic news for women's football in Scotland and something we should all be extremely excited about.

“To welcome the best players in the world to Easter Road would be incredibly special and provide a brilliant opportunity to showcase the women's game. It would also give young girls across the country the chance to experience a World Cup on their doorstep and to see what is possible to achieve through football.

“Having played and coached at Easter Road throughout my career, it holds a very special place in my heart. To see it named as a Candidate Stadium for a Women's World Cup is a hugely proud moment for me, and the opportunity to inspire the next generation makes it even more exciting.”.

Hibs chief executive Dan Barnett added: “The inclusion of Easter Road as a Candidate Stadium for the 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup is fantastic news for the Club and the City of Edinburgh.

According to recent reports, "This is something we've been working hard on for several months, with various positive discussions with the Scottish FA and key stakeholders. In recent years, we have been delighted to host Scotland Women's National Team matches at Easter Road, so to be named as a Candidate Stadium for the finals in 2035 is a huge honour.

“To have the opportunity to showcase our stadium on the world's biggest stage would be an immensely proud moment for the Club. It presents a unique opportunity to welcome tens of thousands of supporters from across the world to Edinburgh and create a lasting legacy for the women's game.

"We're excited by the next steps and the prospect of working alongside the Scottish FA, the City of Edinburgh Council and our partners to help bring this opportunity to life.”.

Recent findings suggest that the bid team projected the tournament would attract 3.5 billion viewers worldwide, and that 4.5 million tickets would be sold. FIFA’s evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

The tournament will feature 48 nations and 104 matches across 39 days, with the final host cities and stadiums to be confirmed by FIFA in due course.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:38 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • This is all becoming rather inevitable at Bournemouth.
  • Nine wins on the bounce for the first time in their history, their victory here against Nottingham Forest making it six on the spin at home at an aggregate score of 15 to nil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:38 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 21 November 2026.

This is all becoming rather inevitable at Bournemouth. Will they ever stop winning? Will Evanilson ever stop scoring?

The numbers alone are astonishing. Nine wins on the bounce for the first time in their history, their victory here against Nottingham Forest making it six on the spin at home at an aggregate score of 15 to nil. Five wins in a row in the Premier League for the first time, too, a result that moved them into the top four.

This is Bournemouth, remember. Only this is Bournemouth now.

Make no mistake: this is no hot streak. This is not a team under Marco Rose carried to win after win after win on a wave of momentum and vibes. This is relentless, breathtaking stuff. This is a team that, week after week, outplays every team that stands in front of them. It doesn’t matter if it’s Forest, or Manchester United, or AC Milan. Bournemouth turn up and they blow their opponents away.

They move it quicker and sharper, they win it back faster and higher. They give teams no time to think or breathe, so it’s little wonder they have no answer.

According to recent reports, ‘We never really struggled, said Rose. 'We suffered a little bit at the end, but we defended quite well together, and that's why it's a deserved win.

Bournemouth racked up their sixth successive league victory and ninth in all competitions.

'If we use the right approach every game – and this is really, really demanding – we win games. Next game, we have to prove it again. If we do it, then we can keep the level up. But as I said, this is a tough job.

In a recent development, ‘The collective is strong, but even this we have to maintain. Because if you win games…I mean, some of our players right now are in a lot of noise and rumours.

'If we are able to keep these kinds of things away from the locker room, and if everyone comes into training every day, works hard and gives everything for the club and the team, then we are really, really good.'.

The only real surprise was that Evanilson, Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian, didn’t leave with more than just his one, now customary, goal.

That itself was another fine finish after Tyler Adams won the ball high up the pitch – obviously – dinked it across to James Hill, back after his first England call-up, who flicked a header into Evanilson’s path. He thumped it past Matz Sels to do the rest.

Rose, who called him a ‘real No9’ the other week, had been urging him to get into the box more to finish off chances. He did that, all right. Twice earlier in the game, he raced on to through balls only to be denied by Sels and a last-ditch tackle from Jair Cunha.

His opening strike, his eighth goal in his last nine games, means he is the first Premier League player to reach double figures for goal contributions with six goals alongside his four other assists. He leads the press, he creates chances, he scores goals. He does the lot.

In a recent development, that’s now six league games in a row he’s found the net, halfway to breaking Jamie Vardy’s record of 11 in a row. You wouldn’t put it past him.

Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian Evanilson scored for the sixth successive league match.

It has been revealed that forest came into this, after all, off the back of a huge, much-needed victory against Manchester City. After just one win in Oliver Glasner’s opening nine league games, that was the performance those around Forest felt that could spark the season into life.

It was also meant to be the one where Liam Delap’s Forest career burst into life with two thunderous goals in a bullying, battering-ram showing.

Alas, they both ran into a proper team this week.

Forest tried to go direct to Delap, partly to try to bypass the intense Bournemouth press, but nothing stuck. Delap lost possession with 23 of his 39 touches. He committed more fouls than he had shots and found his way into the referee’s book for clumsily bundling over Adam Smith.

Sources indicate that the visitors huffed and puffed in the second half but never really looked like scoring. The closest they got was a couple of speculative long-range efforts from Morgan Gibbs-White and James McAtee before a late goalmouth scramble nearly provided an opening through chaos more than creativity.

It was only the busy hands of Sels that kept the scoring respectable.

Recent findings suggest that ’The defeat was deserved,’ said Glasner. ‘City and today were completely different. It's like a different sport. This is football, but it's different.

Sources indicate that 'When teams play like City, when it's more of a tactical game, we are doing well. When it's more of a physical, intense game, we're struggling. Today our weaknesses came to the surface.’.

When asked if he had the players to play this way, Glasner responded: 'Right now, I have to say no. If not, we will add players. If we believe we need somebody to add this physicality, these quick solutions, we will do it.'.

Did they expect much else, though? Forest never beat Bournemouth. That’s 13 meetings in a row now they have failed to win.

‘Nottingham Forest, it’s happened again,’ sang the home fans in the final few minutes.

Liam Delap and Nottingham Forest crashed into a proper team as they came back down to earth after their win over Man City before the international break.

Marcus Tavernier's performances could get a chance with England if he maintains his form.

Sources indicate that bournemouth have already had a couple of deserved England call-ups this season in Hill and midfielder Alex Scott. How long until Marcus Tavernier gets his chance?

No English player has scored more Premier League goals this season than the Bournemouth winger, level with Morgan Rogers and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and once again he was at the heart of everything good the Cherries do.

His superb cross behind the Forest defence found Justin Kluivert for Bournemouth’s second of the afternoon. He danced through the Forest defence to set up Rayan for a late chance.

'It was my 11th Premier League game today, and I couldn't see better offensive midfielders so far this season,’ said Rose.

‘If you see how he works and how he plays, the quality he has, he scores goals. He's 27, he's at the best age.

‘If he plays well, if he stays healthy, I think, like with Hilly, these things come. They're just around the corner.'.

Jamie McGrath has dismissed the idea Hibs players do not enjoying playing at home as they bid to halt a 10-game run without victory at Easter Road in the William Hill Premiership.

The Hibees have not won a league game on their own turf since defeating Kilmarnock 3-0 in early April and their supporters turned on them during a grim 4-0 defeat by Dundee United on Saturday that left them second bottom of the table.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

If they fail to beat Dundee on Tuesday, the winless streak in Leith will extend beyond the eight-month mark.

According to recent reports, “I don’t know,” stated midfielder McGrath on why he thought they were struggling for results at Easter Road. “Personally, I always like playing at home. I love the pitch, I love the stadium. It’s a big open pitch, which I think should suit us. But for whatever reason, so far this season we haven’t been able to capitalise on playing at home.

According to recent reports, “It’s hard to put your finger on one certain thing. Maybe just being more decisive in both boxes or probably conceding goals at crucial times in the game, like after five minutes on Saturday, we just give ourselves a bit of a mountain to climb. It’s hard to put your finger on it, but it’s something that we’re trying to put right.”.

After a difficult start to the season which resulted in Marink Reedijk replacing David Gray as manager in late September, it looked like Hibs had turned the corner when they followed up a rousing victory over city rivals Hearts in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final with a 4-0 win at Aberdeen in their last game before the international break.

Sources indicate that mcGrath, therefore, is hopeful Saturday’s aberration will prove a blip. “We’ve been on a decent run the last month and probably the international break came at a tricky time for us,” said the Republic of Ireland international. Or not a tricky time, but we were just kind of building momentum and had two good wins back-to-back against two good teams.

“It’s frustrating not to build on that, but hopefully we can put Saturday down to a bad day and get back on track.”.

McGrath is unfazed by Hibs being 11th in the table as he senses a chance to change that with three matches in the space of nine days against other sides in the bottom six.

“It’s not something that we’re concerned about at the minute,” he mentioned. “It’s obviously not where we want to be.

“We want to try to get closer to that top six and this two-week period is quite crucial in terms of there being nine points in the next week up for grabs. If you put a little run together, you can boost yourself right up the league.

“It’s just about finding that consistency to hopefully propel us up the league.”.

Bognor took the lead on three minutes as Carter set up Hunphrey on the wing and she placed it low to Delillis, who diverted it in at the near post.

Industry observers note that alice Gue was fouled outside the area. Up stepped Niamh Andersson to take the free-kick but she sent it just over.

According to recent reports, nicole Robinson had to stop Dot Usher’s attempt at the other end. Then Carter squared the ball towards Freya Boxer but she was put off by a defender.

Boxer spotted the keeper off her line and struck it from the far right but it rolled wide. Bognor had to defend with Usher causing problems and two strikes led to two good saves from Robinson.

Delillis had the ball in the net after Carter's through ball but was ruled offside. Macie Downs won a corner with her long throw into the box but a Varsity defender headed away.

Lou Lou Robson came on for Sophia Poling and soon had to head a corner clear before Jess Nunn's strike was saved by Robinson.

Bognor got their third on 63 minutes as Delillis played a pass through defence to Humphrey and she ran into the box and sent the ball to the back post where Carter was waiting to smash it in.

Sources indicate that abbie Akhopie hit a dangerous cross into the area and Robinson had to save before Carter cleared the rebound. Clara Castanheira replaced Gue for the Rockettes then Andersson set up Boxer, but with only the keeper to beat, she fired wide.

Selvester's corner fell to Delillis and she struck the crossbar before Andersson smashed wide on the follow-up.

Sources indicate that bognor concede on 75 minutes as Akhopie sped through following a long ball and fired it in. Soon Delillis played it inside for Humphrey who turned and composed herself but shot wide.

Bower hit a long range free-kick at goal but Robinson denied her. On 80 minutes Poppy Shine replaced Robinson in goal for Bognor. Then on 83 minutes, Boxer came off for Talliah Anderson.

On 93 minutes Andersson came off for Chloe Blanks in Bognor's final change.

Bognor’s win leaves them second, three points behind leaders Havant with a game in hand.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Anthony Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 00:01, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 04:43.
  • Hoping to pick up where they left off prior to the international break, LASK Linz will travel to face Bodo/Glimt at Aspmyra Stadion for a Champions League league-phase showdown on Tuesday.
  • Glimt are hoping to climb into the playoff spots, while the Black-Whites are looking to push closer to the top eight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 00:01, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 04:43.

Hoping to pick up where they left off prior to the international break, LASK Linz will travel to face Bodo/Glimt at Aspmyra Stadion for a Champions League league-phase showdown on Tuesday.

Glimt are hoping to climb into the playoff spots, while the Black-Whites are looking to push closer to the top eight.

Kjetil Knutsen's Bodo/Glimt have endured a difficult European campaign to date, winning just one of their four Champions League outings, beating Borussia Dortmund 1-0 in mid-October.

On November 3, Glimt were held to a 0-0 stalemate by Ligue 1's Lille, blanking for the second time in the league phase as part of a concerning trend that has seen the team muster the joint third worst goal tally in the competition, with only PSV and Slovan Bratislava netting fewer than their four.

That frustrating draw has left Knutsen's side 25th in the Champions League table with just four points, though they are level with all of the clubs up to 20th-placed Roma.

Additionally, Bodo/Glimt are a mere two points shy of their opponents, and will be optimistic about their chances of climbing up into one of the playoff qualification spots in midweek.

With that aim in mind, fans of the hosts will be buoyed by their team's record on home turf, where they have lost just one of their 15 outings across all competitions since early May, winning 13 times in the process.

Meanwhile, Dietmar Kuhbauer's LASK kicked off their league phase with two defeats, but have bounced back in impressive fashion to record consecutive wins ahead of Tuesday's clash.

Last time out in the Champions League, the Austrian champions hammered Slovan Bratislava 4-0 in Linz, racing into a 3-0 lead by half time courtesy of a brace from Kasper Jorgensen and a follow-up by Robert Ljubicic.

That victory came as part of a run that has seen Kuhbauer's men net at least four goals in three of their past five matches, and considering they have scored 10 in UEFA's premier club competition, they are likely to pose a threat in midweek.

On the other hand, LASK have conceded nine times across their four Champions League games so far - the joint second worst total in the top 18 - and they will need to be wary of surrendering chances on the road.

The visitors arrive 16th in the table with six points, a tally that puts them two points clear of 25th-placed Bodo/Glimt and three short of eighth-placed Liverpool.

Bodo/Glimt Champions League form:.

Bodo/Glimt form (all competitions):.

LASK Linz Champions League form:.

LASK Linz form (all competitions):.

Bodo/Glimt will be without midfielder Hakon Evjen, who unfortunately suffered further damage to his cruciate ligament while recovering from a previous knee injury, and could reportedly be sidelined for the rest of the season.

In his absence, Patrick Berg, Sondre Fet and Sondre Auklend look set to start in the centre of the park, platforming a front three of Jens Petter Hauge, Ole Didrik Blomberg and Andreas Helmersen, while August Mikkelsen is dealing with a groin glitch.

Elsewhere, backup goalkeeper Isak Sjong is a doubt, though Nikita Haikin should be ready to line up between the sticks on Tuesday.

As for LASK, they are missing injured left-back George Bello, so expect to see Yvan Dibango and Kasper Jorgensen operate as wing-backs, either side of a three-man defence featuring Xavier Mbuyamba, Andres Andrade and Alemao.

The visitors also have question marks about the fitness of right-sided attacker Moses Usor, and if he is unavailable, Christoph Lang should join Samuel Adeniran up top in midweek.

Bodo/Glimt possible starting lineup:.

Haikin; Sjovold, Gundersen, Bjortuft, Bjorkan; Berg, Fet, Auklend; Blomberg, Hauge; Helmersen.

LASK Linz possible starting lineup:.

Jungwirth; Mbuyamba, Andrade, Alemao; Bogarde; Jorgensen, Dibango; Ljubicic, Horvath; Lang, Adeniran.

Bodo/Glimt may have found wins hard to come by in the Champions League, but they are unbeaten on home turf in the competition and could prove stubborn opposition once again.

LASK will be confident going forward, though their defensive frailty could cost them at least two points on Tuesday.

It has been revealed that the 53-year-old has had little time to ponder his future. "It has been a tough 24, 48 hours," said Pressley. "There’s a lot of embarrassment, a lot of disappointment.".

He stressed there was also a determination to learn from the most challenging experience of his managerial career. Although he has spoken before of coming close to walking away on at least two occasions last season, resigning had not crossed his mind this time.
