Upcoming system, same problems: Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace ends in defeat despite tactical switch... but Coventry are up to 13th

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.
  • It has been revealed that there were, however, some noticeable improvements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.

Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.

It has been revealed that there were, however, some noticeable improvements. Palace were more structured in attack, with cleverly orchestrated moves and a clear, coherent plan for creating chances.

In a recent development, but the same problem that plagued his predecessor Pierre Sage persisted: Palace cannot defend. That diagnosis is simple to make. However, addressing it is complicated by inadequate personnel.

Palace replaced Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix with teenage defender Honest Ahanor and Chelsea castoff Axel Disasi in the summer.

Until they can address the oversight in their squad planning - thinking that would be enough to replace two international centre-backs - they will continue to ship sloppy goals.

Frank will be able to address the structural problems, ensure players understand the positions they should occupy in specific situations and get Palace defending as a cohesive unit.

These are all things within his control and he began fixing them to some extent on Saturday.

Despite having a upcoming manager in the dugout, the same old problems remained for Crystal Palace.

His in-game management worked to a degree as Palace conceded two goals and defended frantically in the first half before looking much more solid and organised in the second period before finally conceding the decisive goal in the 85th minute.

What he won’t be able to eradicate, though, are the individual errors that have consistently cost Palace this season.

Ultimately, those mistakes come down to the quality of the defenders at his disposal.

Palace will look to address their personnel issues in January but they currently sit rock bottom of the league, with a massive game against Hull next Sunday.

Unless they can cut out the errors that have contributed to their 27 league goals conceded this season, they risk being cut adrift before they can bring in reinforcements.

Recent findings suggest that upcoming boss Frank was more glass-half-full, though. ‘There is more positive than negative from the game,’ Frank remarked. ‘We looked like a threat. We scored two very good goals and we created quite a few more chances to score at least one more goal.

‘That was the big positive. I was extremely happy with the effort and the mentality of the players.’.

In a recent development, defensively, this was a horror show. Three players were dragged out wide — including Disasi, who was miles out of position — allowing Jack Rudoni to find Taiwo Awoniyi in the penalty area to poke past Dean Henderson four minutes into Frank’s first assignment.

Coventry should have had a second, too, after Palace overcommitted in attack and Awoniyi was played in behind. One-on-one with Dean Henderson, he took the ball around the goalkeeper, only for Axel Disasi to somehow get back and clear it off the line.

Palace had been on the front foot but were caught out by how quickly they had to transition from attack to defence, unable to get enough bodies back in time. They are struggling to find a balance between defence and attack.

Dwight McNeil's own goal cost Palace late on as they slumped to a 3-2 defeat.

Industry observers note that anan Khalaili failed to win his tackle for Coventry’s second, giving Rudoni space to run down the right. Nobody shut Rudoni down and he found Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, who rocketed a thunderous half-volley into the top corner from outside the area.

Coventry’s 85th-minute winner came from a long throw, which Palace failed to deal with.

Frank abandoned the back three, which had served Palace well for the last two years and nine months, and pivoted to a 4-2-3-1.

Offensively, Palace improved. The formation suited Yeremy Pino and Jorgen Strand Larsen particularly well, with the pair combining for both of Palace’s goals.

It should also bring the best out of Quinten Timber, Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton, as individuals are rarely isolated in midfield, unlike under Pierre Sage.

On the other hand, Tyrick Mitchell and Khalaili still tried to function as wing-backs rather than full-backs.

It has been revealed that that is ingrained in their habits, and it will take time to coach it out of them. However, it remains a significant glitch.

Both players committed themselves forward when attacking, leaving an already fragile centre-back pairing exposed and allowing Coventry to transition rapidly and exploit Palace's vulnerability.

That cannot happen in a back four, as there were situations where Palace had eight players forward with only the goalkeeper and two centre-backs staying back.

Coventry were far from convincing defensively but found a way to beat their relegation rivals, climbing to 13th on 12 points, three clear of the drop zone.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto celebrates scoring Coventry's second with Jack Rudoni.

Frank Lampard’s side have now won four of their last seven games and sit above fellow promoted sides Hull and Ipswich — an impressive feat after losing their first four games back in the Premier League.

The Coventry boss said: ‘It’s a massive win for us. Every win for us in this league is a big win. But when a game is that tight, it’s important to get what we got.

‘After our start, where we played the best three teams in the league, we had zero points after four games, and now where we are is great progression.

Sources indicate that ‘That’s only down to hard work. We are the underdog in most games, so for them to experience and live difficult moments that this league will bring, it will help the players grow.’.

Industry News: The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool

📅 11 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 35 min read (7054 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~35 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered.
  • How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.
  • It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

Industry observers note that this is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

There was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k.

Recent findings suggest that the midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

According to recent reports, this is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

Sources indicate that instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

In a recent development, they are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. Given the tone coming out of the Etihad Stadium, nobody will be acquiescing to any alleged wrongdoing, certainly not on Sunday, but minds were made up on Merseyside about how far City had pushed the boundaries in pursuit of success a long time ago.

Sources indicate that “There has been a lot of talk about various things,” explains John Gibbons, host of Anfield Wrap, the popular Liverpool podcast. “Manchester City trying to say they are going to be hard done to, but there are no great surprises among Liverpool fans about these charges, are there?

“Everyone who goes to the match, who supports Liverpool, have known all along that a lot of those sponsorship deals looked questionable. Did they pass the smell test? That’s why the atmospheres in the past when City came were always brilliant and I’m expecting it will be the same again.”.

So that is why Anfield will be a maelstrom of sound and fury for one of the most significant occasions in Premier League history.

The half-and-half scarves have been replaced by more topical match-day merchandise this afternoon...

Here is what City’s head coach said during his first press conference after the guilty verdict:.

Recent findings suggest that “There is a process ongoing and in this moment I completely trust the club … I trust the club because I trust the people and this is also the reason why I joined the club. And then there is not another club in the world where I would [rather] be.”.

“Absolutely not. The last time I was here was the treble season. I know the effort from the players, from the club, from the manager in that time that was Pep [Guardiola]. I know exactly the effort that the club put to achieve that kind of target.”.

According to recent reports, “I won the Championship with Leicester. League One, we will see, but we are thinking about something that we don’t know.”.

I’m not worried at all. The environment [among] the players is nice. In this moment we are top of the league so the players have all the reason to be happy and excited.

“One hundred per cent… Because I know the organisation from years ago, and I know how serious they are, I know that they do the right things. I would like to speak about this when we win the appeal.”.

While Liverpool have struggled for wins in this fixture of late, it’s worth noting that this run includes five draws.

Liverpool have won just three of their last 13 Premier League clashes with Man City 👀 https://t.co/OxkeDpLjQq.

On Saturday Manchester United fans resurrected their “ticker” mocking Manchester City’s trophy drought following their rivals’ cheating scandal:.

There was also a nod to Rui Pinto, the whistleblower whose Football Leaks documents prompted the Premier League’s investigation into City:.

There were four days between the news leaking that Manchester City had been found guilty of the majority of charges first levelled at them by the Premier League in February 2023 and the independent commission findings dropping.

Staff, then, had had a bit of time to process a guilty verdict although little, it seems, could adequately prepare them for the excoriating tone and content of the commission’s ruling.

“The thing that has shocked me more than anything is the language the commission used to describe the club’s conduct,” one staff member told Telegraph Sport this week.

“We had been waiting for a very long time to see what came out of these Premier League charges and lots of different things go through your head. But I just wasn’t expecting that. I’m still a bit shell-shocked by the ferocity of what the commission stated. I think that’s what’s worried me.”.

"Enjoy the ride and smile" Erling Haaland with a message for Man City fans ahead of their trip to Anfield this weekend 🎙️🩵 https://t.co/H7so0fk6XE.

Industry observers note that “The international break is good because we can review what we have done and what we can do better,” Enzo Maresca said after Manchester City’s harum-scarum 5-3 victory over Sunderland. “But at the same time we can relax a little bit more.” One wonders how much respite Enzo Maresca and Manchester City actually enjoyed in the intervening 21 days.

Since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. Until then, though, the show goes on and City’s players and staff must compete knowing that their every move now comes with a caveat.

City have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca remarked, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

Industry observers note that given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

Arsenal injury news: Raya blow leaves Arteta facing a season-defining dilemma

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:35.
  • Mikel Arteta's concern over David Raya has grown beyond the result of the 2-2 draw with Newcastle on Saturday.
  • Still without a definitive diagnosis, the player is due to undergo tests to determine the severity of the problem, but the possibility of missing a few weeks represents a significant setback for Arsenal's plans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:35.

Mikel Arteta's concern over David Raya has grown beyond the result of the 2-2 draw with Newcastle on Saturday. The Spanish goalkeeper had to leave the pitch in the second half following a collision with William Osula, and has become a source of apprehension at Arsenal.

Still without a definitive diagnosis, the player is due to undergo tests to determine the severity of the problem, but the possibility of missing a few weeks represents a significant setback for Arsenal's plans.

Sources indicate that raya received treatment on the pitch, but continued to show discomfort and was unable to remain in the match. Kepa Arrizabalaga came on in his place, 25 minutes into the second half. In his post-match interview, Arteta did not hide his concern over the situation of his first-choice goalkeeper.

'Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. Tomorrow, he will have an MRI scan, but at the moment I do not know' - the manager remarked.

Sources indicate that the apprehension is understandable. Raya is not just Arsenal's first-choice goalkeeper: he has become a central piece in the way the team organise themselves defensively and start their moves. His security when coming off his line, ability to play with his feet and involvement in build-up from the back make him a reference point within Arteta's model. Finding a replacement capable of reproducing all of these characteristics is no simple task.

Arteta's first alternative is set. Signed to join the squad and provide depth in the position, Kepa is Raya's immediate understudy and took over as soon as the Spaniard had to leave the pitch against Newcastle.

Should the injury rule the first-choice goalkeeper out for a few weeks, the former Real Madrid man will have the opportunity to show that he can sustain the team's competitive level at an important point in the season.

The question, however, involves more than simply filling the spot. Kepa has experience at big clubs and knows the demands of playing decisive matches, but his record also includes episodes that fuel doubts about his consistency. His performance against Newcastle, for example, was not enough to remove the question marks over his ability to take over as first choice without Arsenal suffering a drop in performance.

According to recent reports, the most uncomfortable memory for supporters is the League Cup final last season against Manchester City. On that occasion, a mistake by Kepa carried weight in the result and reinforced the criticism of the goalkeeper.

While an isolated episode does not determine a player's ability, the current situation demands that he offer answers on the pitch, especially if he has to take over the position for a longer period.

Recent findings suggest that the challenge also lies in the differences between the styles of the two Spaniards. Raya offers a combination of reflexes, positioning and quality in distribution that allows Arsenal to maintain their approach even when under opposition pressure. Kepa will need to show security both in his interventions and in his decisions with the ball, preventing the change in goal from causing significant alterations to the defensive functioning.

According to recent reports, in addition to Kepa, Arsenal have Illan Meslier in the squad. The Frenchman appears as another possibility for Arteta, although he is behind the Spaniard in the goalkeeping hierarchy.

His presence widens the options available, but does not necessarily mean the manager is willing to promote an immediate change in the order of preference.

Recent findings suggest that giving Meslier an opportunity would be a decision involving risks and benefits. On the one hand, it would allow Arsenal to assess an alternative in a position that may require more than one player over the course of the season.

On the other, backing a goalkeeper who does not right now occupy the first position in the contest could represent an even bigger change in a system that would already need to adapt to Raya's absence.

The possibility of looking for a reinforcement in the January transfer window may also enter the debate, particularly if the tests confirm a more serious injury and a lengthy recovery period. Even so, signing another goalkeeper would not be an automatic solution. Besides market availability, Arsenal would need to find a player who offered the conditions to take over as first choice and adapt swiftly to Arteta's demands.

The timing of the season makes the situation even more delicate. Arsenal lead the Premier League and also have important commitments in the Champions League. In the coming weeks, the team will face opponents such as Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham and Real Madrid, a sequence that will demand concentration and consistency in every area.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • It has been revealed that luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals.
  • Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026.

It has been revealed that luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' said De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'.

Asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with.

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

You make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

There has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate.

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

In a recent development, spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5).

Scorers: Williams-Barnett, Solanke.

Booked: Maddison, Williams-Barnett, Kudus, Fernandes.

Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6.

Belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

Williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' remarked Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'.

Spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

According to recent reports, they were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

Savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.

PSG: Why Doue's serious injury could derail Luis Enrique's season

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (924 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:48.
  • PSG's 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday at the Allianz Riviera, in round 11 of Ligue 1, brought terrible news for Luis Enrique.
  • It has been revealed that shortly before half-time, Desire Doue, who had scored a goal minutes earlier, collapsed to the ground after twisting his right knee while attempting a dribble.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:48.

PSG's 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday at the Allianz Riviera, in round 11 of Ligue 1, brought terrible news for Luis Enrique.

It has been revealed that shortly before half-time, Desire Doue, who had scored a goal minutes earlier, collapsed to the ground after twisting his right knee while attempting a dribble. Amid cries of pain, the winger had to leave the pitch on a stretcher when substituted.

In a recent development, speaking to Ligue 1+, the Spanish manager stated in advance that Doue's injury 'was serious', a fear confirmed on Sunday. Imaging results found that the PSG number 14 has suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament and will have to undergo surgery in the coming days.

PSG have not disclosed a recovery timeline, but cases similar to Desire Doue's that require surgical intervention show that players usually spend at least six months in the medical department. The 21-year-old Frenchman should therefore only return to action at the end of May.

Industry observers note that in the most optimistic scenario, Doue would be fit in time for a possible Champions League final, to be played on 5 June at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, Spain. However, depending on the strategy PSG adopt to cover for the young winger's absence, the success of this season is at risk.

Signed in August 2024 from Rennes for £42.5m (€50m), Desire Doue became one of Luis Enrique's trusted men, so much so that he was an vital part of the rotation in his debut season (16 goals and 14 assists in 61 matches) and was named man of the match in the European final against Inter Milan, when he scored twice.

According to recent reports, in 2025-26, the French attacking midfielder had his run at PSG interrupted by two muscle injuries, but still managed 13 goals and eight assists in 40 matches, as well as scoring his penalty as PSG won back-to-back Champions League titles against Arsenal. And after representing his country at the World Cup, Doue was enjoying an overwhelming start to the season.

As a reward for his good form at PSG, Doue began to gain more space in the France team under Zinedine Zidane, who even said that he reminded him of himself when he played as a midfielder, because of his personality of always wanting to improve by listening to older players.

More than the impact in the final third, Doue is also a joker for the PSG manager because of his two-footedness, able to play on either wing.

The Frenchman had been playing on the left in recent weeks as a replacement for Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who also suffered an anterior cruciate ligament rupture in his right knee during the win over Barcelona on 20 October, in the Champions League.

The Georgian underwent surgery and should only be available to the Spanish manager in mid-April. With two heavyweight absences in the attacking system, PSG must ask themselves whether it is necessary to reinforce the area when the transfer window reopens, or whether the current squad will be enough to remain competitive on all fronts.

It has been revealed that if PSG conclude that the solution lies in the market, they will have to do very meticulous work to find someone who fits Luis Enrique's playing philosophy, based on high intensity and constant movement, and who is available to leave in January. It is true that there is no shortage of talents around the world who fit those requirements, but the certainty is that no signing would be cheap, nor a guarantee of immediate success.

It has been revealed that on the other hand, if PSG give a vote of confidence to the current players, which at the moment is the public discourse, they will have to get more out of their players. 2025 Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele has suffered from different physical problems in 2026-27, so much so that he has constantly been placed on a load management regime.

Ferran Torres, signed from Barcelona for £42.5m (€50m), had an exciting start at PSG, with seven goals in the first six matches. However, as in his Camp Nou days, the Spanish forward began to fluctuate and went eight games without scoring, ending the drought against Nice.

It has been revealed that maghnes Akliouche, bought from Monaco for £42.5m (€50m), has not yet reached his full potential (two goals and three assists in 16 matches), which is normal for a newcomer. But the lack of prior experience as a protagonist in the Champions League raises doubts over whether the 24-year-old Frenchman is able to make a difference for PSG.

In a recent development, it is a similar case to Mika Godts, acquired from Ajax for £46.8m (€55m), but with the aggravating factor that he is still going through the process of adapting to French football. As he is still 21, the Belgian winger has been inconsistent at PSG, with two goals and two assists in 12 matches.

Finally, Senny Mayulu (20) and Quentin Ndjantou (19) are academy gems still looking to establish themselves among the professionals. The Spanish manager does have the possibility of pushing Nuno Mendes and/or Achraf Hakimi forward, but that would create a problem at full-back.

PSG have seven more games until the winter break, but with Ligue 1, the Coupe de France and the Intercontinental Cup, it is undeniable that the mission of chasing a third successive Champions League title has become much harder without Doue.

Cole Palmer was involved in an angry exchange with Joao Pedro after the final whistle of Chelsea’s woeful home defeat to Leeds United.

Xabi Alonso’s side were thrashed 4-1 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon with the visitors scoring three times in the second-half to seal a famous win in the capital.

Emmanuel Emegha opened the scoring for the hosts after 25 minutes before Noah Okafor levelled the contest three minutes later.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin put Leeds back in front eight minutes into the second-half before Okafor added his second of the afternoon.

Brenden Aaronson wrapped things up with a fine solo effort in added time to seal win that moved Leeds ahead of Chelsea in the Premier League table.

Pedro was not in the squad, still recovering from a thigh injury that has now ruled him out of Chelsea’s last five games.

It had been hoped he would be fit after the international break but Xabi Alonso revealed on Friday the striker was still not back in training.

The Brazil international was in attendance on Saturday afternoon and was involved in a tense exchange with one of his teammates immediately after the game.

The Athletic report Palmer appeared to have an angry exchange of words with Pedro as he left the pitch.

During Alonso’s post-match press conference, one journalist suggested the disagreement was sparked when Pedro tried to get Palmer to go and applaud the fans with the England international seemingly reluctant.

Alonso said of the incident: ‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I said, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still so long way to go..

Palmer had played the full 90 minutes but was unable to inspire his side who have now won just one of their last five games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Dominik Szoboszlai always knew Florian Wirtz's qualities would eventually shine through for Liverpool after delivering a "world-class" performance against Manchester United.

Wirtz produced one of his most impressive displays since joining the Reds from Bayer Leverkusen last summer in Sunday's 4-0 thrashing of Mauricio Pochettino's side at Anfield.

After Szoboszlai opened the scoring from a free-kick following Leny Yoro's red card, Wirtz doubled Liverpool's lead in the 13th with a superb volley from inside the penalty area.

Liverpool could have pulled further clear, but both Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola wasted presentable opportunities, both of which were teed up by the impressive Wirtz.

Rio Ngumoha got himself on the scoresheet in the 66th minute before Wirtz found Victor Munoz, who took a touch before concluding the rout eight minutes from time.

Wirtz created 10 open-play chances against United, the most by a player in a Premier League match since Manchester City's David Silva against West Brom in March 2015 (11).

He now has eight goal involvements (three goals, five assists) in all competitions in 2026-27, and Szoboszlai believes the Germany international is only just getting started.

"I always knew he was a good player," Szoboszlai mentioned. "He's world-class. I love to play with him. We understand each other very well.

"I think we are similar types of guys who understand the game in the same way. That's why it's easier for us.

It has been revealed that "Now he's in the flow, scoring against [Crystal] Palace, for the national team and scoring another goal. So yeah, we need him, and he knows that, and he will shine even more.".

10 – Florian Wirtz created 10 chances in open play against Manchester United, the most by a player in a Premier League match since David Silva v West Brom in March 2015 (11). Unlocked. https://t.co/q0DzqlFMZJ.

Wirtz now ranks either first or joint-first in the Premier League in November for goal involvements (four), expected assists (1.28), chances created (11), defensive line-breaking passes (12), and possession won in the final third (five).

But another fine performance came from the lively Ngumoha, who, aged 18 years and 85 days, became the youngest player to score and assist in a Premier League game for Liverpool since Michael Owen on Boxing Day 1997 (18y 12d v Leeds United).

"Everyone knows how good he is, and he is doing it every week in the games and day by day in the training, because if he wasn't, he may not get the chance," Szoboszlai added.

According to recent reports, "So you have to show yourself in the training sessions, show it to the gaffer and then you get the chance. He is doing that every time and, yeah, he is still young with lots to learn.

Sources indicate that "The sky is the limit for him. I think his career is like [on an upward trajectory] until now, and now he has to be clever and listen maybe to the older players who have a little bit more experience. Some of us more, some of us less.

"We try to help him, but it's also two parts. He's young, he's 18, so it's a long way to go, and he has to be ready for everything, the ups and downs.

"He cannot be really up when he's up, but also when he's down a little bit, he cannot be really down, so he has to find the balance.".

Glenn Murray believes Bruno Fernandes will look to leave the club if he doesn’t sign a newly introduced Manchester United contract before the January transfer window.

Fernandes won the PFA Players’ Player of the Year last year after a superb second half of the season under Michael Carrick, but has not hit those same heights so far this campaign.

The Red Devils captain was also dropped for a game after publicly criticising Carrick’s tactics following a heavy Champions League defeat to Como.

The arrival of Mauricio Pochettino represents a fresh start for Fernandes this season, but there remains uncertainty over his long-term future at the club given the 32-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season.

Fernandes has already turned down two contract offers from the club, and former Brighton striker Murray believes he could be eyeing up a move away from Old Trafford when the transfer window reopens in January.

‘I wouldn’t burst the bank [on a upcoming contract] for him,’ Murray told Sky Sports. ‘I think he’s not the future of the football club.

‘Listen, he’s given his best years to Manchester United and unfortunately they haven’t won an awful lot, which he would have liked.

‘I think if he gets the option to move on, and it gets to January, and he can start speaking to other people, I think it will open his eyes up to see where he could go and if he could win things and finish off his career more enjoyably, because there have been years at Manchester United that have been really difficult.

‘He has been the standout player, but he is not the future and it could be time to part ways.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dominic Calvert-Lewin believes Chelsea’s players could not handle the ‘intensity’ during Leeds United’s 4-1 win at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Chelsea took the lead in the first half through an excellent finish from Emmanuel Emegha but Xabi Alonso’s side were in front for just three minutes as Noah Okafor pulled Leeds level.

Leeds then came out flying in the second half and Leeds were given a penalty after Jayden Bogle’s thumping strike hit Rogers on the top of his arm.

Calvert-Lewin converted the spot-kick to put Leeds ahead and Daniel Farke’s side continued their dominance in the second half as Okafor netted his second of the game before Brenden Aaronson completed the deserved victory with a goal in injury time.

Chelsea have now been beaten in three out of their last four Premier League games, while only Coventry City, Ipswich Town and Crystal Palace have conceded more goals than Xabi Alonso’s side this season.

During his post-match interview with Sky Sports, Calvert-Lewin was asked what the message was from Farke during the half-time break with Chelsea already showing signs of fragility.

It has been revealed that ‘The message was just more of the same. I think we were going well, we just weren’t putting our chances away and we knew the next chance was coming and we’d have to take it,’ Calvert-Lewin replied.

‘To be honest, I expected Chelsea to come out with a bit more oomph in the second half but I think our intensity, the way that we played and the way we set up against them, they couldn’t handle it, and I think that reflected in the scoreline.’.

Asked what the message was ahead of the game against Chelsea, Calvert-Lewin replied: ‘Intensity, bring the intensity from the start.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manchester United's hierarchy have been accused of negligence by former captain Gary Neville after failing to strengthen their defence during the summer transfer window.
  • The Red Devils slumped to a concerning latest low as they suffered a humbling 4-0 defeat against rivals Liverpool on Sunday, leaving them 19th in the Premier League table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:10, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 11:22.

Manchester United's hierarchy have been accused of negligence by former captain Gary Neville after failing to strengthen their defence during the summer transfer window.

The Red Devils slumped to a concerning latest low as they suffered a humbling 4-0 defeat against rivals Liverpool on Sunday, leaving them 19th in the Premier League table.

Latest head coach Mauricio Pochettino became the first boss in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his opening match in charge of a club.

Liverpool took advantage of Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card and ran riot on Merseyside, with goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz condemning the Red Devils to their fifth league loss of the season.

Man United have posted only one win in 11 league games this season, while they have now conceded 34 goals across all competitions – the highest total of any team across Europe's top-five divisions.

Commenting on Man United’s defensive woes as a pundit for Sky Sports, Neville mentioned: "It's negligent. The negligence is not bringing in defenders in the transfer window, because we've seen this for two or three years.".

Man United instead opted to prioritise a midfield rebuild, with Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans all brought in for a combined fee in the region of £150m.

Pochettino’s nightmare start to life as Man United boss could not have gone much worse, and his decision to hand Matthias de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days has been called into question by Neville.

The Dutch defender, who recently recovered from a long-term injury, was partly at fault for the first goal conceded by the Red Devils, misjudging a high ball that led to Yoro’s red card, and he was run ragged by Liverpool’s pacey frontline all afternoon.

"[Myself and Jamie Carragher] were in the trucks over in the compound and when the team came through straight away we were very surprised," said Neville.

Industry observers note that "I just didn't think Manchester United would win, and I thought they would concede lots of goals and make mistakes. Maybe the options on the bench aren't brilliant either, but it's really desperate and it's tiring watching them.

Industry observers note that "Mauricio Pochettino's options are not great, but I didn't get De Ligt. Having been out for a year myself, it's really difficult to come back into a game like that.

Sources indicate that "I'm not saying that you can't, but as a centre-back getting your bearings… You saw him in Como (4-1 defeat in the Champions League), he was all over the place in Como. It's almost like you don't know what's happening.

In a recent development, "I found that coming back into it when I was 32, he's obviously more experienced as well. I was very surprised he played but then the others haven't been doing great either.".

While Neville believes that a back four of Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw (currently injured) represents the “best” back four for Man United, playing with other defensive combinations will see the club get relegated.

In a recent development, "You wonder how low it can get, but this is as low as it's been in 54 years," Neville added. "A few weeks ago against Fulham, I said it's the worst 40 minutes or 30 minutes I've seen in my lifetime.

Recent findings suggest that "At the time people said that was maybe a bit too much, but this is actually the worst Manchester United have ever been in 54 years. It's a fact. The worst defensive team in Europe, second bottom in the league, they've never started this badly.".

It has been revealed that he continued: "I would have started with Harry Maguire today. Manchester United's best back four - and I think we're informed enough to know, we've watched these lads for two or three years - is [Luke] Shaw, Dalot, Maguire and Martinez.

"Now, it's a poor back four, let me be really clear. But it is Manchester United's best back four.

"Now, if you can get that back four out on the pitch, it does win games, against Liverpool last year, it does win games against City and Arsenal, it can compete slightly.

"But that back four that started today, and the one that finished against Villa a few weeks ago of [Noussair] Mazraoui, [Patrick] Dorgu, Yoro, and [Ayden] Heaven - that will get you relegated, that's a fact.".

Man United’s total of just eight Premier League points after 11 matches is their lowest at this stage of a top-flight season since 1972-73, but Pochettino’s side are only one point adrift of safety heading into their next league fixture at home to Brentford on Saturday.

#95331. How to make AI data centres more sustainable

How to make AI data centres more sustainable

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1325 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M.
  • Around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence.
  • People have many concerns about the way AI is being developed, including how it might affect safety, security and jobs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M. Santiago/Getty.

Around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence. Communities worry that existing infrastructure will not be able to handle the surge in demand for electricity and water, and that data centres’ energy demands will cause environmental and health problems, including increases in air pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions. The question of whether AI is going to stall climate action is explored in the first of a three-part Nature Podcast (Nature https://doi.org/rzqs; 2026).

Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

People have many concerns about the way AI is being developed, including how it might affect safety, security and jobs. Where energy is concerned, however, any added demand for computing power can, and must, be met in smart, sustainable ways, not by burning more fossil fuels. Achieving this will take some creative thinking, and researchers need to be closely involved. Many argue that there are alternatives to relying on energy-intensive data centres, such as AI models that can run on individual computers or institutional servers, thereby consuming much less power than those run using cloud services. Efforts to develop such options need to be better funded.

It has been revealed that future projections of data centres’ energy demands are hard to make, because they are based on assumptions that could change. If current global trends continue, electricity consumption by data centres will go on rising. Between 2017 and 2024, it grew by around 12% per year. Figures for 2024 from the International Energy Agency (IEA), based in Paris, show most of this demand coming from three regions: the United States (45%), China (25%) and Europe (15%).

According to recent reports, the Electric Power Research Institute, a non-profit organization in Palo Alto, California, has projected that the continued growth of US data centres could add up to 94 gigawatts of demand by 2030, equivalent to 17% of the country’s electricity consumption. Data centres currently consume more than 1.5% of the world’s electricity supply, and the IEA’s projections indicate that this figure will more than double in the next few years. By 2030, data centres could consume more electricity than Japan, the agency says.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Sources indicate that there are serious concerns that this extra demand will be powered mainly by fossil fuels, when carbon emissions are already at a record high. Research published this week in Nature Sustainability estimates that some 400 data centres in the United States accounted for around 26 megatonnes of carbon dioxide emissions between May 2024 and April 2025, more than those produced by many countries (G. Guidi et al. Nature Sustain. https://doi.org/hcsptc; 2026). And according to a study published last week in Nature Climate Change, data centres’ energy demands could prolong the lifespan of coal-fired power stations (C. Li et al. Nature Clim. Change https://doi.org/rzqr; 2026).

But none of this is inevitable. Governments could mandate that fresh energy demand be met with renewable sources. And regulators could look at alternative ways to manage existing electric supplies.

Many nations’ electric grid systems are designed to accommodate surges in demand, whether to power extra cooling on hot summer days or extra heating during winter cold snaps. Much of the time, there is excess capacity. This excess could be used to reduce the amount of fresh energy needed to power data centres.

How much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

Recent findings suggest that how much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

According to recent reports, one solution is to curtail data-centre operations during periods of peak electricity consumption, and ramp up at times of lower demand. An analysis released in 2025 by researchers at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina, found that the US electric grid could accommodate 98 gigawatts of extra demand in this way, without adding any new generation capacity (see go.nature.com/4cdeknm). That 98 gigawatts would be enough to cover most, if not all, of the expected expansion in US data centres over the next few years.

There is potential for this to become a reality. In June, as part of a larger effort to modernize the grid, the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission instructed grid operators to draw up a proposal for how they will cope with extra demand from data centres. The technology industry is understandably paying close attention to how it might mitigate the problems of powering data centres. Earlier this month, OpenAI unveiled what it is calling a “grid protectors program”, a project to consult with US grid operators, regulators and policymakers to see how the organization can work around peaks in power demand.

Meanwhile, Google is paying households and businesses in parts of the Eastern United States to reduce their electricity consumption during periods of high demand. Similar proposals are being considered in other countries.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

These are all tentative moves in the right direction, although arguably progress is not being made fast enough. Policymakers and data-centre operators must engage seriously with those who oppose the centres’ expansion. At a minimum, any new energy sources developed to power these centres must be renewable. Existing energy sources can also be better deployed, and researchers working to develop alternatives to energy-intensive data centres should be better supported. More peer-reviewed evidence is needed, especially for countries outside the United States.

According to recent reports, there are smarter and more sustainable ways to power the growth of AI, but to achieve them, concerted and coordinated action will be needed. In this way, the harm posed to people and the planet can be minimized, and AI technologies can benefit everyone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:30, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 08:31.

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro is forced to serve a suspension following his early red card in Sunday’s heavy 4-0 defeat at Liverpool in the Premier League.

The 21-year-old defender was named in Mauricio Pochettino’s first starting lineup as the new Red Devils head coach, operating on the right side of a three-man defence.

However, his afternoon came to an abrupt end inside the first eight minutes when he was shown a straight red card for a clumsy coming-together with Liverpool striker Alexander Isak on the edge of Man United’s penalty area.

Defensive partner Matthijs de Ligt – starting his first PL game in 357 days – misjudged a high ball by Ronald Araujo, which gifted Isak a free run towards goal before Yoro brought him down as the last man.

At the time of the incident, referee Sam Barrott said on-field: "It's a red card for DOGSO (denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity). On-field decision is outside [the box], red card, DOGSO," to which VAR added: "Defender bundles into him into the back, gets too tight, I think it's a foul.".

The Premier League Match Centre then explained the decision, posting on X: "The referee’s call of red card to Yoro for denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity (DOGSO) was checked and confirmed by VAR.".

According to recent reports, leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! ? https://t.co/VKYvckvBBP.

This is the second time that Yoro has been sent off for Man United this season, having previously been giving his marching orders in a 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid in October for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Yoro’s dismissal at Anfield was immediately punished, as Dominik Szoboszlai fired home the resulting free kick, before Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead less than three minutes later.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz then got their names on the scoresheet in the second half to help Liverpool secure a comfortable victory against a Red Devils outfit that sit down in 19th place in the Premier League table after 11 games.

Yoro will now serve a one-match suspension in the Premier League, forcing him to miss next Saturday’s clash against Brentford at Old Trafford, before he is free to return for a trip to Newcastle United on December 2.

Red cards for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity - a non-violent offence - carries a standard one-game domestic suspension rather than a three-match ban.

Before the Red Devils face Brentford, they will take on Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday and Yoro is available to play for Pochettino’s side in that game, as he served his UCL ban in the previous fixture against Roma at the start of the month.

Pochettino led a chorus of complaints that Yoro was given an “unfair” red card at Anfield, telling Sky Sports: "So painful. So disappointed. It's not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

"The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it's so painful.

"The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

"We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.".

Industry observers note that pressed on whether he was unhappy with Isak's heavy touch, Pochettino: "The ball was for the goalkeeper (Senne Lammens). In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, [Yoro] never had the intention to connect with Isak.

It has been revealed that “When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down. In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional.".

Man United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo agreed with his new manager, adding: "The game's been taken out of our hands by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.

In a recent development, "No chance. The ball's already with the goalkeeper. They're both running full speed. What can we do? It is what it is.

"It's 10 versus 11, you come to a place like Anfield, it's a tough game anyway. Then you lose a man, it makes it hard. I can't fault the boys for their fight in the game. We take the pain and move on.

"I wouldn't say it all goes out the window. You can still take the things you did in training into the game, but it makes it 10 times harder with one less man in a situation like that.

"It's hard, it's painful. But no one's coming to save us. We have to work hard, keep digging, keep working, keep fighting. It will all come round.".

Meanwhile, Gary Neville has questioned one key decision made by Pochettino in his first Man United match and has hit out at the club’s 'negligent' hierarchy over their summer transfer dealings.

Feyenoord and Porto meet at De Kuip on Tuesday night with both clubs under pressure to revive their Champions League campaigns.

Recent findings suggest that having collected just three points from their opening four league-phase matches, the Dutch side sit 32nd in the 36-team table, while Porto are only slightly better off in 26th place. With the knockout rounds already beginning to drift out of sight for both teams, victory could prove pivotal.

Feyenoord head into the contest in poor form and desperately searching for a positive result after six matches without a win in all competitions.

Their latest setback came at the weekend when they were beaten 3-2 at home by Excelsior, a result made all the more painful by the fact it marked Excelsior’s first league victory at De Kuip in 46 years. Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s side began brightly through an early goal from Givairo Read, but three unanswered goals left Jan Plug’s late strike as little more than a consolation.

The defeat followed a 5-3 loss away to Heerenveen and a 3-0 home defeat to Inter Milan in the Champions League, meaning Feyenoord have conceded at least three goals in each of their last three matches.

Defensive concerns have become a major glitch. The Dutch club have now lost 10 of their last 13 European fixtures and have conceded the opening goal in each of their last seven Champions League outings. That sequence includes defeats against Barcelona, Real Betis and Inter Milan, with their only victory in the current campaign coming against Como.

With memories of last season’s disappointing Europa League campaign, when they finished 29th in the league phase, another defeat would leave their hopes of reaching the knockout stages hanging by a thread.

Anis Hadj Moussa is being assessed after returning from international duty with an ankle injury that forced him to miss the defeat against Excelsior.

Tsuyoshi Watanabe is also a doubt after being substituted at half-time on Saturday with a foot problem.

Jakub Moder and Bart Nieuwkoop remain unavailable through injury, while Thomas Beelen, Jordan Bos and Jerry St. Juste are all expected to miss out as well, leaving Van Bronckhorst short of defensive options.

Former Arsenal winger Reiss Nelson made his first start for the club at the weekend, but Luciano Valente could be recalled on the left flank for Tuesday’s encounter.

Porto arrive in Rotterdam with considerably more momentum despite their difficult start to the Champions League campaign.

Industry observers note that francesco Farioli’s side finally claimed their first victory of the league phase on matchday four, producing an emphatic 4-1 win over Napoli. Jan Bednarek, Gabri Veiga, Jakub Kiwior and Samu Omorodion all found the net as the Portuguese side responded impressively after losing their opening three European matches against Manchester City, Real Betis and PSV Eindhoven.

Domestic form has been excellent. Porto have won all 11 of their Primeira Liga matches and already hold a five-point lead at the top of the table. Their most recent outing was less straightforward, though, as they required a penalty shootout to overcome third-tier Paredes in the Taca de Portugal after a 1-1 draw across 120 minutes, due to an extremely unusual own-goal.

The Dragons are competing in the Champions League main stage for the first time in three years and are hoping to reach the knockout rounds for the third consecutive appearance.

However, their record in the Netherlands offers some encouragement for Feyenoord. Porto have failed to win any of their past four away matches against Dutch opponents, drawing two and losing two. Their previous visits to De Kuip ended in a draw in 1993 and a 2-0 defeat in 2019.

It has been revealed that vasco Sousa remains sidelined with a long-term leg injury. Former Manchester United defender Chris Smalling is struggling with a knee issue and is also ineligible, having not been included in Porto’s Champions League squad.

William Gomes has returned to training after recovering from an ankle problem, but his involvement remains uncertain.

Midfielder In-beom Hwang is set for an emotional return against his former club after joining Porto from Feyenoord during the summer, while striker Santiago Gimenez is also returning to Rotterdam after representing Feyenoord between 2022 and 2025.

Feyenoord’s defensive struggles make it difficult to back the hosts with confidence, particularly against a Porto side carrying significantly stronger form and fresh confidence following their dominant victory over Napoli.

While De Kuip remains a challenging venue and Porto’s historical record in the Netherlands is far from convincing, the visitors appear better equipped to handle the pressure of such a crucial European fixture. Given Feyenoord’s recent performances and recurring defensive issues, Porto look capable of taking advantage and securing an vital away victory.

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:50.

Tottenham Hotspur have received a major patch on the future of teenage starlet Luca Williams-Barnett.

The highly-rated academy graduate, who turned 18 at the start of October, made a notable impression on his full debut for Spurs in a 2-0 Premier League home win over Ipswich Town last weekend.

Williams-Barnett opened the scoring with his first senior goal in the 15th minute, arriving at the back post to poke the ball home, before a blistering dribble that began from inside his own half helped him to set up Dominic Solanke shortly after half time.

Tottenham’s youngest scorer in the Premier League since Gareth Bale in 2007 received a standing ovation from the home crowd and also picked up the Man of the Match award.

After making his first-team debut as a 16-year-old last season, calls for the skilful winger to get more minutes have only grown louder over a challenging 12 months at Spurs.

Ensuring that Williams-Barnett commits his future to the club has also been high on the agenda, with the youngster having now entered the final 24 months of his current deal.

However, football.london reports that Williams-Barnett has agreed to sign a fresh long-term deal at Tottenham, seemingly cooling fears that he could leave to join a rival club.

The England Under-19 international has now featured four times in the senior Spurs side under head coach Roberto De Zerbi, who was full of praise for the “special” teenager after the win over Ipswich.

"Luca is a special player,” De Zerbi told reporters post-match. "I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top teammates.

"I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important.

"The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom, and Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

"And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

"Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch.".

After revealed that Williams-Barnett prepared for the game on the team bus by watching YouTube videos of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar, De Zerbi was asked whether the Spurs starlet could reach the same level as Barcelona and Spain sensation Yamal, who finished third in the 2026 Ballon d’Or rankings.

De Zerbi replied: "Yes, I think so, and one of the best things in my career… I've seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

"I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?".

Williams-Barnett will hope to be rewarded with a second successive start when Tottenham travel to the Stadium of Light to face Sunderland in their next Premier League fixture on Sunday.

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EST, 21 November 2026.

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed midfield duo Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan after the recalled pair both scored in the 4-1 home win over St Mirren.

With Mika Baur facing 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill handed McCowan his second start of the season and Oxlade-Chamberlain his fifth, as the two joined forces for the first time.

Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan netted either side of Camilo Duran in a nine-minute flurry of goals late in the first half with Callum McGregor making it four for Celtic in the second period before Killian Phillips reduced the deficit for Saints from the penalty spot.

According to recent reports, O’Neill mentioned: ‘Alex has been waiting around for a while to get into the side. He’s a brilliant passer of the ball. He took his goal very well with a calm finish in the bottom corner.

‘He was feeling a little bit sore, so taking him off was just precautionary.

Sources indicate that ‘I was also delighted Luke got his goal. That should give him a boost in confidence.’.

Oxlade-Chamberlain congratulates McCowan after he scored to make it three for Celtic.

McCowan faced criticism after Celtic’s Champions League collapse against LASK and his only previous start this season saw him taken off at half-time in a home defeat by Rangers.

O’Neill said: ‘I thought he did really well, also playing the full game given it has been some considerable time since he has done that.

According to recent reports, ‘He got the ball early on and played it almost blindly and it was intercepted and I thought, “oh, gosh, here we go”. But he roared back, took his goal well and I am really pleased for him. He is a real genuine lad.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It has been tough for him. In the game against Rangers, he was thrown into a position, and it didn’t start well for him in the match. I think he felt it was deja vu for him in terms of the game at the back end of last season too. That will be good for him.’.

The Celtic manager also introduced 19-year-old former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joel van den Berg for a debut in the second half.

‘I thought he did very well,’ said O’Neill. ‘He’s coming on after an injury which kept him out for some time.

‘I am pleased there is a bit of competition for places now.’.

The veteran midfielder celebrates his strike that opened the scoring against St Mirren.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish felt Celtic were clinical in his team’s heavy defeat in Glasgow.

‘It’s a really sore one with the way the scoreline ended up,’ noted McLeish.

‘I thought we started the game quite well and then that flurry of goals can happen here when you’re playing against such a strong team. The difference was the quality in our box compared to theirs.

‘They are just so clinical, and they get into those good areas and they punish you.

It has been revealed that ‘I felt we got into some similar areas throughout the game. We didn’t give up, we didn’t move away from what we were trying to do, but we were just really lacking that final bit.’.

Manchester United have hired former Arsenal coach Sam Wilson, who has already started work as part of Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff.

Wilson left Arsenal in the summer, having been at the club for 12 years.

He was the lead physical performance coach under Mikel Arteta up until the end of last season, playing his part in Arsenal’s Premier League title-winning season.

Wilson left the Gunners as part of the club’s overhaul of their medical department, with significant changes made in an attempt to address the injury problems that have hindered the squad in recent seasons.

After departing his role at Arsenal, Wilson briefly joined Parma, where he was appointed head of performance by Arteta’s former assistant Carlos Cuesta.

Industry observers note that however, Cuesta was sacked in September and Wilson left the club a month later. He has now made a swift return to England.

Wilson was on the bench at Anfield on Sunday as Pochettino took charge of United for the first time.

He has joined United as a first-team fitness coach and will play his part in what is expected to be a key focus of Pochettino’s reign.

United rank second-last in the running stats in the Premier League this season, in stark contrast to the stats recorded by Pochettino’s teams at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

During his time at Arsenal, Wilson oversaw a lot of the individual training work with players returning from injury complications.

When Bukayo Saka came back from injury to face Fulham last year and scored within seven minutes, he ran straight to Wilson on the bench to celebrate with him.

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

According to recent reports, it was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

Sources indicate that matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

Industry observers note that “It was an outstanding performance,” the manager mentioned. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

In a recent development, the win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

In a recent development, even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.
